title: Find Peak Element
description:
A peak element is an element that is strictly greater than its neighbors.

Given a **0-indexed** integer array `nums`, find a peak element, and return its index. If the array contains multiple peaks, return the index to any of the peaks.

You may imagine that `nums[-1] = nums[n] = -∞`. In other words, an element is always considered to be strictly greater than a neighbor that is outside the array.

You must write an algorithm that runs in **O(log n)** time.

examples.explanation: 3 is a peak element and your function should return the index number 2.
Your function can return either index 1 (peak 2) or index 5 (peak 6).

constraints: nums[i] != nums[i + 1] for all valid i
hints: If nums[mid] < nums[mid + 1], there must be a peak to the right.
If nums[mid] > nums[mid + 1], there's a peak to the left (including mid).
This is because the edges are -∞, so a peak is guaranteed to exist on the ascending side.

solutions.explanation: Binary search: if nums[mid] < nums[mid+1], a peak must exist on the right (ascending). Otherwise, a peak must exist on the left (including mid). Converge to the peak.

dryRunSteps.explanation: Find peak in [1,2,3,1]. Initialize left=0, right=3.
mid=1, nums[1]=2 < nums[2]=3. Ascending → peak must be on the right. left = mid+1 = 2.
mid=2, nums[2]=3 > nums[3]=1. Descending → peak is on the left (including mid). right = mid = 2.
left=right=2. Return 2. nums[2]=3 is the peak! 🎯

realWorldUseCases.description: Finding local maxima in signal data (audio waveforms, stock prices) efficiently using binary search on gradient direction.
